cause.reason: the evaluation kernel was created with enable_gpu:false, so Kaggle served a CPU-only image whose torch build string differs from the CUDA image used for training (which computed on CPU regardless)

guard_assessment: The frozen evaluator's runtime check worked exactly as intended. It caught an infrastructure divergence that would otherwise have produced an unreproducible result, and it caught it before consuming the partition.

one_shot_accounting.assessment: The scientific property the one-shot seal protects - that no development-derived information can influence any decision - is INTACT, because the evaluator aborted before reading a single development record and produced no output. The transfer itself is recorded here rather than hidden.
one_shot_accounting.gate_treated_as: UNSPENT, with this transfer event disclosed

remedy.change: recreate the evaluation kernel with enable_gpu:true so the image supplies torch 2.10.0+cu128 / cuda 12.8, while still passing --device cpu so the numerics match training exactly

what_happened: The sealed development partition was transferred into the kernel and hash-authenticated (dev 9c893d8e..., manifest 47ee157a...). The frozen evaluator then REFUSED to run, raising EvidenceQueryEvaluationError('canonical H3 evaluation runtime must match training') before reading any development record.
